title: Peak Power Prediction of Lithium-Ion Battery Considering Long Discharge Time for Trains Under Emergency Traction
abstract: When an electric multiple unit (EMU) loses catenary supply, the on-board energy-storage system must simultaneously sustain auxiliary loads and provide sufficient traction power for the train to reach a safe stopping location. In this situation, the available battery power is not constant over a long discharge interval because the state of charge (SOC), terminal voltage, and equivalent-circuit parameters evolve continuously. This study develops a long-horizon state-of-power (SOP) prediction framework for emergency traction. An emergency power-flow model first links battery power to traction-motor demand and auxiliary consumption. A second-order RC model is then combined with fast recursive least squares (FRLS) for online SOC and parameter estimation, while offline SOC-dependent parameter functions are used to update the battery model inside the SOP prediction horizon. On this basis, the peak discharge current is determined under battery-design, SOC, and terminal-voltage constraints by an iterative binary-search procedure. The resulting SOP is further mapped to the available emergency traction force. The validation includes the 25 ∘C LTO-cell tests together with low-SOC, multi-temperature, method-comparison, ablation, route-stress, and pack-level analyses. These results show that updating the equivalent-circuit parameters inside the prediction horizon materially changes the long-horizon power limit relative to a fixed-parameter formulation, while the binary-search implementation retains a computational structure suitable for train-borne use.

title: Impact of Electrical Parameter Measurement Error on Battery SOC Estimation Accuracy and Compensation Strategies
abstract: The estimation accuracy of the battery state of charge (SOC) directly affects the reliable and stable operation of the battery management system (BMS). In complex operating conditions such as vehicle-mounted applications and energy storage power stations, systematic biases and random noise are common in voltage and current sensing measurement. Most existing studies on SOC error focus on the independent effect of individual measurement error and lack systematic explanation on the propagation mechanism and quantitative influence of multi-source errors. In this paper, based on the second-order RC equivalent circuit model, the analytical transfer model of SOC estimation error is established under the framework of the extended Kalman filter (EKF), and the transfer path of measurement error in the algorithm is clarified. Then, a battery test bench with “reference-measurement” dual-channel parallel measurement is built. Under the constant-current discharge condition, the contribution weight quantification and sensitivity analysis of multi-source measurement error to SOC estimation error are completed, and it is revealed that the voltage measurement bias is the dominant error source of SOC estimation. On this basis, an augmented-state modified EKF algorithm (AM-EKF) with online identification of voltage bias is proposed. The voltage measurement bias is incorporated into the state vector to realize the joint estimation and online compensation of the operating state and measurement bias. The results show that under the constant-current discharge condition, the improved algorithm increases the proportion of SOC estimation error within the ±3% qualified interval to more than 85% in the whole discharge period. The maximum estimation error is significantly lower than that of the traditional EKF algorithm, and the accuracy is close to the unbiased ideal condition. Under the modified DST dynamic condition, the improved algorithm controls the SOC estimation error within 5%, which is 72% lower than the traditional EKF calculation error with bias input. The scheme has high robustness, no additional hardware cost, controllable computational complexity and excellent engineering application value.

title: Beyond standard battery testing: a physics-informed framework for validating next-generation battery packs
abstract: Standardized battery testing provides an essential foundation for benchmarking and qualification, yet its ability to represent increasingly complex operating conditions is becoming limited. Existing protocols provide reproducible measures of electrochemical performance but often evaluate individual stress factors under controlled laboratory conditions, which may not fully capture the coupled physical environments encountered in real-world operation. Global electric-vehicle battery demand is projected to exceed 3 TW h by 2030, more than tripling from around 1 TW h in 2024 under the IEA Stated Policies Scenario, highlighting the need for reliable battery qualification. As battery technologies evolve toward cell-to-pack architectures, fast charging, solid-state systems, and intelligent battery management, the gap between standardized testing and operational reality is becoming more pronounced. This perspective develops a conceptual physics-informed validation philosophy and proposes a six-level Validation Maturity Framework, progressing from protocol-oriented testing toward stress-oriented, mechanism-oriented, physics-informed, and predictive validation. Representative studies report prediction errors ranging from 2.93% under previously unseen temperatures to below 0.5% on independent datasets, illustrating the quantitative potential of physics-informed and data-driven approaches when validation extends beyond conventional operating conditions. The framework emphasizes physical relevance and mechanistic understanding rather than increasing experimental complexity alone, and discusses how mechanistic models, real-time sensing, physics-informed artificial intelligence, and digital twins can support predictive battery qualification. Standardized testing therefore remains the foundation of a broader validation hierarchy for improving the reliability and practical qualification of next-generation battery packs.

title: Digital twin of a battery for traction rolling stock and substations: remaining useful life estimation based on a dual Kalman filter
abstract: Background: One of the key objectives of digital transformation in railway transport is the development of digital platforms and digital twins aimed at improving operational efficiency. Predicting the remaining useful life of equipment is a critical task for traction rolling stock and traction substations of traction power supply systems. A key component affecting the reliability of these assets is batteries. The development of a digital twin of a battery for traction rolling stock and substations enables the estimation of essential parameters, namely remaining capacity and remaining useful life (RUL). Aim: To develop a digital twin of a battery for traction rolling stock and traction substations of traction power supply systems, providing estimates of remaining capacity and RUL based on a dual Kalman filter, using a mixed approach to state-of-charge (SoC) estimation and adaptive forgetting factors derived from measurements of current, voltage, and temperature. Materials and methods: To achieve the stated aim, the research employed methods of experimental design, mathematical statistics, differential calculus, and a dual Kalman filter algorithm. Verification of the results was performed using experimental data from a lithium-ion battery with a series connection of 15 cells. The estimation of remaining capacity and RUL was based on joint filtering of the parameters of a Thevenin equivalent circuit model and the SoC. Results: A digital twin of a battery for traction rolling stock and substations has been developed. The proposed digital twin enables the determination of remaining capacity and RUL from measured values of current, voltage, and temperature. Conclusion: The results were verified against measurement data from standard control and monitoring systems. The mean absolute percentage error for the SoC and voltage estimation was less than 1.5% and 0.5%, respectively. The obtained estimates of the RUL and remaining capacity are reliable and consistent with the results of similar studies in charge–discharge cycles. The proposed method for estimating the remaining useful life and remaining capacity of batteries for traction rolling stock and substations is recommended for use in technical condition monitoring and diagnostic systems within the framework of the Digital Locomotive and Digital Substation projects.
title_zh: 牵引机车与牵引变电所电池数字孪生：基于双卡尔曼滤波的剩余使用寿命估计
one_sentence: 构建面向牵引机车与变电所电池的数字孪生，采用双卡尔曼滤波联合估计 SOC、剩余容量与 RUL。
problem: 牵引供电与机车储能设备的电池剩余容量与 RUL 难以从常规监测数据中直接获取，缺乏可在线运行的联合状态-参数估计方案。
contributions: 构建基于 Thevenin 等效电路与 SoC 混合估计方法的电池数字孪生
采用双卡尔曼滤波与自适应遗忘因子实现参数与 SoC 的联合滤波，估计剩余容量与 RUL
用 15 节串联锂离子电池实验数据进行验证，并与标准监控系统测量结果对比
bms_relevance: 直接涉及 BMS 的 SOC 估计、RUL 预测与数字孪生架构，串联电池组场景与 pack 级管理相关。
insight_for_group: 双卡尔曼滤波联合估计参数与状态的方案可参考用于课题组 pack 级 SOH/RUL 数字孪生实现；但其验证规模较小（15 串单体），可作为 baseline 思路而非主要依据。
reason: B级。Modern Transportation Systems and Technologies 为小众期刊，不在优先列表内，证据规模有限；但数字孪生 + 双卡尔曼 RUL 估计与课题组方向相关，建议浏览。

title: Battery State of Health Estimation Using a Hierarchical Gradient Algorithm Under Varying Temperature Conditions
abstract: Abstract Accurate state-of-health (SOH) estimation of lithium-ion batteries under varying temperature conditions is essential for safe and efficient battery management systems (BMSs).However, conventional empirical SOH models often neglect temperature-dependent aging, while variable projection (VP)-based identification requires repeated projection and matrix-factorization operations.To address these issues, this paper proposes a temperature-coupled double-exponential SOH model and a hierarchical gradient (HG) algorithm for efficient parameter identification.An Arrhenius-type temperature factor is embedded in the degradation-rate terms to represent temperature-dependent electrochemical aging reflected by capacity fading.The HG algorithm alternately updates the linear and nonlinear parameter blocks through a Gauss--Seidel-type gradient scheme, thereby avoiding repeated projection calculations.Identification results under staircase temperature conditions show that HG achieves accuracy comparable to VP in terms of RMSE and the coefficient of determination, while substantially reducing computational time.The proposed method provides a lightweight temperature-aware SOH estimation scheme for resource-constrained BMS applications.
title_zh: 变温条件下基于层次梯度算法的电池健康状态估计
one_sentence: 提出温度耦合双指数 SOH 模型与层次梯度算法，在变温条件下实现轻量化 SOH 估计。
problem: 传统经验 SOH 模型忽略温度相关老化，而变投影类辨识方法需要反复投影与矩阵分解，计算负担重，难以用于资源受限 BMS。
contributions: 构建嵌入 Arrhenius 型温度因子的双指数 SOH 退化模型
提出 Gauss-Seidel 型层次梯度算法，交替更新线性与非线性参数块，避免重复投影计算
在阶梯温度工况下验证精度与变投影相当，同时显著降低计算时间
bms_relevance: 面向 BMS 的 SOH 估计与温度相关老化建模，强调轻量化实现，符合车载 BMS 算力受限的实际需求。
insight_for_group: 其温度耦合退化模型与轻量化在线辨识思路，可用于课题组 SOH/RUL 算法在边缘 BMS 上的部署优化；层次梯度结构也可与 cloud-edge 架构下的端侧计算需求结合。
reason: B级。Journal of The Electrochemical Society 不在优先列表内，期刊层级中等；方法在温度相关 SOH 建模与计算效率上有可取之处，建议浏览。
